programmes.name: Sustainability and Tourism
programmes.description: Explore how tourism affects places, communities and the environment.
programmes.curriculum: Tourism, sustainable society, research methods, languages and a final project.
programmes.practical: Off-campus study and internship options are documented; places and extra costs need checking.

programmes.name: International Studies
programmes.duration: 4 years including preliminary year; 3-year entry depends on qualification
programmes.credits: 120 Nottingham credits in preliminary year; confirm full degree total
programmes.description: Explore politics, history and how countries and societies interact.
programmes.curriculum: Academic English, politics and history, then thematic options and a dissertation.
programmes.practical: Seminars and a supervised final research project; no guaranteed internship verified.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.description: Learn to build software and understand algorithms and computer systems.
programmes.curriculum: Computing foundations, algorithms, data systems, software design and electives.
programmes.practical: Mandatory industrial attachment, group design projects and a final-year capstone.

programmes.name: Industrial Design
programmes.duration: 4 years; English preparation can add 1 year
programmes.description: Design useful products by combining creativity, materials and how people use things.
programmes.curriculum: Design studios, materials, manufacturing, ergonomics, design history and communication.
programmes.practical: Final-year studios collaborate with industry; confirm summer-practice rules.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.description: Explore behaviour, the brain and evidence-based ways to support people.
programmes.curriculum: Psychology, research and statistics; choose mental health and wellbeing or applied psychology.
programmes.practical: Laboratory and research learning; further study is required to register as a psychologist.

programmes.name: Environmental Sciences
programmes.description: Investigate how people affect water, land, biodiversity and climate.
programmes.curriculum: Ecology, earth sciences and environmental chemistry within a flexible science degree.
programmes.practical: Laboratory work and field trips in freshwater, coastal and forest environments.
programmes.campus: Hamilton or Tauranga; confirm paper locations

routes.name: Kazakhstan Attestat through preliminary year
routes.eligibility: Grade 11 Attestat normally enters the preliminary year; typical average 4 with 5 in relevant subjects. Individual assessment and English evidence still apply.
routes.recognition: Kazakhstan Grade 11 Attestat is explicitly listed for preliminary-year entry; this is not direct entry to year two.
routes.subjects: Confirm which subjects must carry grade 5 for International Studies.

routes.name: Kazakhstan school certificate plus AP or A-level qualifications
routes.eligibility: Ordinary Kazakhstan school certificate needs at least 3 AP tests with grades 4 and 5, or at least 3 qualifying UK A-level subjects. Subject and timing rules apply; this is extra preparation.
routes.recognition: Ordinary Kazakhstan certificate alone is not accepted for direct admission. NIS Grade 12 is a separate qualification route.
routes.subjects: Confirm the current Mathematics, Physics or Computing subject equivalents before choosing AP or A-level subjects.

ENGLISH.detail: English test required if school teaching was not in English or English is ESL/EAL; an approved schooling exemption is conditional.

IELTS.detail: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, writing 6.5 and speaking 6.5 is one accepted English route.

SAT.detail: SAT 1250 with Reading and Writing 600 is an English-evidence option; it does not replace the additional AP/A-level requirement.

tuition.note: Current international tuition and any Tuition Grant obligations were not verified.

routes.mandatoryFees: Mandatory fees and insurance need a current quote.
routes.nextAction: Check additional qualification subjects and costs before planning an NTU application.

routes.name: Kazakhstan UNT primary-qualification route
routes.eligibility: Published Kazakhstan minimum: UNT 125/140 in five subjects including two relevant profile subjects. Meet citizenship, diploma and holistic review conditions; the minimum does not guarantee admission.
routes.recognition: UNT is explicitly accepted as a primary application document. Exact diploma recognition and registration documentation still need confirmation.
routes.subjects: Two UNT profile subjects must relate to the programme; ask which combination applies to Industrial Design.

UNT.detail: 125/140 in five subjects for this chosen primary-qualification route.

SAT.detail: SAT is not required when applying with the accepted Kazakhstan UNT route.

ENGLISH.detail: No external English score is obligatory at application. After admission, use an accepted result or METU English exam; failing proficiency can add a one-year English preparatory class.

IELTS.detail: IELTS taken on or after 24 December 2022 is not accepted; do not book it for METU exemption.

tuition.note: 2026/27 reference: USD 1200 per semester, shown as USD 2400 for two semesters. Pay in TRY under official conversion and floor rules; 2027/28 fee is unverified.

routes.mandatoryFees: English preparatory students pay the same faculty tuition; insurance and other fees need checking.
routes.nextAction: Ask METU to confirm Industrial Design profile subjects and the next intake rules.
questions: Confirm the exact qualification, applicant category and selected intake with admissions.

routes.name: International applicant with an approved pre-university qualification
routes.eligibility: Meet an accepted pre-university qualification score, Mathematics and science prerequisites, age rules and English evidence. Ordinary Kazakhstan Grade 11 acceptance is not established.
routes.recognition: Exact Kazakh diploma equivalence is unknown; an approved foundation may add time and cost.
routes.subjects: Mathematics and one science: credit average at Australian Year 11 equivalent or pass average at Year 12 equivalent.

ENGLISH.detail: Accepted English study, English-medium schooling, approved tests or Monash English may meet the rule; documentary evidence and time limits apply.

IELTS.detail: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall and 6.0 in each component; other accepted measures are listed.

tuition.note: Published international tuition per year in 2027, before applicable service tax and extra charges.

routes.mandatoryFees: MYR 100 application, MYR 200 registration, MYR 100 amenities per semester; student-pass fee extra. International tuition and related fees carry 6% service tax.
routes.nextAction: Request a qualification assessment and full 2027 international fee quote including tax.

awards.name: UNNC Provost International Excellence 100% Scholarship
awards.benefits: 100% of first-year tuition only; later tuition and all living costs remain.
awards.eligibility: Full-time international undergraduate offer holders; competitive selection.
awards.application: Submit a scholarship statement of up to 500 words through the application hub; confirm the selected-cycle deadline.
awards.renewal: Entry award for first year only; not automatically renewable.
awards.upfront: Tuition can be waived or refunded if already paid; visa, insurance and living costs remain.

awards.name: Waikato Vice-Chancellor’s International Excellence Scholarship
awards.benefits: 2027 regulations: NZD 8000–15000 tuition credit; no living support.
awards.eligibility: New full-time international student, offer of place and at least B+ equivalent. Must not qualify for a country-specific version; current Waikato/College students, sponsored and exchange routes are excluded.
awards.application: Apply after receiving an offer, before paying tuition or applying for a visa. Offshore A-trimester applicants must apply before 30 November; B-trimester before 31 May. Confirm the year and cutoff.
awards.renewal: 12-month award; retain full-time on-campus international status and the offered qualification.
awards.upfront: Do not pay tuition or apply for a visa before the scholarship application; remaining tuition, insurance, travel and living costs need funding.
